items.title: MyCC: Cartel whistleblowers to get stronger protection, rewards
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Malaysia Competition Commission (MyCC) will strengthen protection and provide rewards to whistleblowers who provide information on cartel activities or bid-rigging practices. MyCC chief executive officer Datuk Iskandar Ismail said stronger protection was crucial as cartel activities typically occurred secretly and behind the scenes, requiring the cooperation of whistleblowers connected to companies or consumers. Iskandar said, once the amendments are gazetted this year, MyCC will be able to provide more comprehensive protection to individuals who come forward with information.

items.title: China-Malaysia ties reach new heights after three major elevations - Outgoing ambassador
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: China-Malaysia relations have undergone three major elevations over the past five years, culminating in a high-level strategic community with a shared future, outgoing China's Ambassador to Malaysia Ouyang Yujing said. Ouyang said Chinese President Xi Jinping's state visit to Malaysia in April marked another milestone in bilateral ties, ushering in what he described as a new "Golden 50 Years" for China-Malaysia relations. "His Excellency's meeting with Premier Li Qiang yielded important new consensus for deepening win-win cooperation between our two countries," Ouyang said.

items.summary: TAMPIN: A married couple died in an accident involving two vehicles on Jalan Gemencheh today. items.title: US says no China arms sale plans after envoy cites Trump offer
items.summary: WASHINGTON: The United States said Monday that it has no plans to sell arms to China, after a US envoy said President Donald Trump asked Xi Jinping if he would like to buy American weapons. US Ambassador to China David Perdue said Trump made the extraordinary offer to sell arms to the rival superpower in response to Chinese concerns over weapons sales to Taiwan. Trump's proposal came during Chinese President Xi's pomp-filled state visit to the White House last week, Perdue told Fox News.

items.title: Seoul says North Korean mines 'highly suspected' as cause of DMZ blast
items.summary: SEOUL: A blast that injured three South Korean military officers inside the Demilitarised Zone (DMZ) last week was likely caused by North Korean landmines, Seoul's military said Monday. The preliminary findings of a joint probe with the United Nations Command into the Sept 21 explosion suggested that "recently planted mines" were involved, Kwon Dae-won, vice chairman of South Korea's Joint Chiefs of Staff, said at a live briefing. "The mines exploded at a location about 10m south of the Military Demarcation Line, and we have confirmed that the site was about 10m from an area where changes in the terrain were observed and where North Korean forces are believed to have recently planted mines," he said.

items.title: 5 Malaysians nabbed in Jakarta for smuggling drugs in their shoes
items.summary: JAKARTA: Five Malaysians were detained by the Indonesian police (Polri) Criminal Investigation Agency (Bareskrim) on Friday for smuggling 5kg of the synthetic drug etomidate concealed in their shoes. Polri Narcotics Eradication Division director General Eko Hadi Santoso said the suspects were searched after Indonesian Customs and Excise officers became suspicious of the movements of the five individuals. Police seized seized various raw materials and equipment for assembling vape pods, including 16 five-litre jerry cans of flavouring liquid, five one-litre bottles of liquid, 21,000 empty vape pods and 15,000 silicone pod caps.

items.title: Foreign leaders pay tribute to Siti Hasmah's medical, public health legacy
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Condolences from foreign leaders continued to pour in following the passing of Tun Dr Siti Hasmah Mohd Ali, with tributes highlighting her lifelong contributions to medicine, public health and social welfare. Pakistan President Asif Ali Zardari expressed deep sorrow over her passing and extended his heartfelt condolences to former prime minister Tun Dr Mahathir Mohamad, his family and the people of Malaysia. "Dr Siti Hasmah's long and distinguished service in medicine, public health and social welfare would be remembered with respect," Zardari said, according to Pakistan's Press Information Department (PID).

items.title: China, US agree tariff cuts on US$60bil of goods including agriculture, household items
items.summary: BEIJING: China and the United States have agreed to cut tariffs imposed on US$60 billion worth of goods imported from each other, on an array of products ranging from US corn to cosmetics, and from Chinese household appliances to toys. Under the US-China Board of Trade, both countries have each recommended US$30 billion of trade in non-sensitive goods for more favourable tariff treatment, US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer said in a statement on Sunday. For the United States, that was "unlocking improved market access" for about 30 per cent of US exports to China, he said.

The other plaintiffs are Affinity Equity International Partners Limited, Alsen Chance Holdings Limited, BlackRock Commodities (Global) Limited, Blackstone Asia Real Estate Partners Limited and Brightstone Jewellery Limited.

items.title: Roti canai maker charged in Kota Tinggi court with murder of five‑year‑old niece at Tanjung Sedili river
items.summary: KOTA TINGGI, Sept 28 — A roti canai maker was charged in the Magistrate’s Court here today with the murder of his five-year-old niece in Kampung Padang, Tanjung Sedili, here last week. No plea was recorded from Abadi Mohd Yasro, 37, after the charge was read out before Magistrate Nur Najihah Hamidi, as the case is triable by the High Court. According to the charge sheet, the father of three allegedly murdered Putri Nur Affiya Qhalhesya Shahrul, five, at about 8.20am on Sept 21 at a river in Kampung Padang, Tanjung Sedili, Kota Tinggi.

items.title: Economy Minister Akmal says RM2,000 minimum wage decision rests with PM Anwar in Budget 2027
items.summary: He also said that the Federal Government had allocated RM127 million under Rolling Plan 1 (RP1) of the 13th Malaysia Plan (13MP) for the repair and maintenance of police quarters and stations nationwide. Akmal Nasrullah said the allocation included an additional RM5 million through a Notice of Change (NOC), bringing the total allocation to RM127 million from the original RM122 million. Of the total, RM44.35 million was allocated for the repair and maintenance of police stations, while RM77.65 million was for the repair and maintenance of 3,716 quarters nationwide.

items.title: Wan Junaidi, Hajiji extend condolences to Dr Mahathir over Dr Hasmah’s death
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 28 — Leaders in Sabah and Sarawak have extended their condolences to former Prime Minister Tun Dr Mahathir Mohamad and his family following the death of his wife, Tun Dr Siti Hasmah Mohd Ali, today. In Kuching, Sarawak Governor Tun Dr Wan Junaidi Tuanku Jaafar and his wife, Toh Puan Fauziah Mohd Sanusi, paid tribute to Tun Dr Siti Hasmah’s contributions to medicine and public health. In Kota Kinabalu, Sabah Chief Minister Datuk Seri Hajiji Noor described Tun Dr Siti Hasmah’s death as a profound loss felt not only by Dr Mahathir and their family but by Malaysians across the country.

items.title: Dr Hasmah was ‘mother figure’ to 1992 Thomas Cup squad, says Razif Sidek
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 28 — National badminton legend Datuk Razif Sidek described the passing of Tun Dr Siti Hasmah Mohd Ali as a great loss to the Malaysian badminton family, particularly the members of the 1992 Thomas Cup squad who ended the country’s 25-year wait for the prestigious trophy 34 years ago. He said Tun Dr Siti Hasmah’s presence in Barcelona was particularly meaningful to the national badminton players, especially for the support and encouragement she provided throughout the Games. “Alhamdulillah, we managed to bring home the country’s first Olympic medal at the time,” said Razif, who last met Tun Dr Siti Hasmah last year.

items.title: Police maintain 24‑hour presence at Najib’s Langgak Duta home pending further instructions
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 28 — Security at the residence of former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak in Jalan Langgak Duta here is still being maintained around the clock, said Kuala Lumpur Police Chief Datuk Fadil Marsus. He was speaking after attending the handover ceremony for the Kuala Lumpur Special Branch chief and Dang Wangi district police chief at the Kuala Lumpur Police Contingent Headquarters (IPK) today. Fadil said the security detail at the residence involves personnel from the Sentul District Police Headquarters (IPD) and the Kuala Lumpur IPK.

items.title: N. Sembilan royal crisis: Former exco members arrive at MAINS Tower to give statements to Bukit Aman team
items.summary: SEREMBAN, Sept 28 — Several former Negeri Sembilan State Executive Council (Exco) members have arrived at the Negeri Sembilan Islamic Religious Council (MAINS) Tower here to have their statements recorded by a Bukit Aman team, following the current crisis in the state. Among the former Exco members are Datuk Faizal Ramli, Mohd Fairuz Mohd Isa, Datuk Mustapha Nagoor, Siti Nur Umaira binti Hasim, Suhaimizan Bizar, and Datuk Razali Abu Samah; they arrived separately starting at 10am today. It is understood that police personnel and officers have also arrived at the tower to record the statements of the former Exco members.
